model.name: Expense reimbursement
model.documentation: Employee expense reimbursement from submission through correction, required approvals, payment, or rejection.

flows.name: Incomplete
flows.condition: The claim is missing required receipts.

flows.name: Complete
flows.condition: The claim contains the required receipts.

flows.name: EUR 2,000 or below
flows.condition: Claim amount is less than or equal to EUR 2,000.

flows.name: Above EUR 2,000
flows.condition: Claim amount is greater than EUR 2,000.

flows.name: Above EUR 2,000
flows.condition: Claim amount is greater than EUR 2,000.

flows.name: Approved
flows.condition: The line manager approves the business purpose.

flows.name: Rejected
flows.condition: The line manager rejects the business purpose.

flows.name: Approved
flows.condition: The Finance Controller approves the high-value claim.

flows.name: Rejected
flows.condition: The Finance Controller rejects the high-value claim.

evidence.summary: Employees submit claims; Accounts Payable checks receipts and returns incomplete claims; the line manager approves business purpose; claims above EUR 2,000 also require Finance Controller approval; Accounts Payable pays approved claims and informs the employee; rejected claims end with a notice.
The employee submits the expense form with receipt images, corrects the same claim when incomplete, and receives a notice when it is rejected or paid.

The line manager decides business purpose; Finance Controller approval is also required above EUR 2,000; no approval order is prescribed; Accounts Payable pays only after every required approval is present.

Accounts Payable checks required receipts; incomplete claims loop for same-claim correction; business-purpose approval is required; claims above EUR 2,000 additionally require Finance Controller approval without prescribed order; Accounts Payable records payment or rejection and sends the corresponding employee notice.

decisions.description: Represent incomplete-claim correction as a loop back to receipt checking under the same claim identity.
Use an inclusive split and join so line-manager approval is always selected and Finance Controller approval is additionally selected above the threshold, without prescribing an order between them.
A rejection ends the claim and terminates any other active approval branch after Accounts Payable records the rejection and notifies the employee.

links.assertion: The employee submits the expense claim.
Accounts Payable checks required receipts.
An incomplete claim is corrected under the same identity and checked again.
Required approvals are selected without imposing an order.
The line manager approves business purpose for every claim.
Finance Controller approval is required above EUR 2,000.
Payment waits until every selected approval is present.
Accounts Payable records rejection and notifies the employee.
Accounts Payable pays approved claims.
Accounts Payable sends the employee the payment notice.

scenarios.name: Complete claim at or below EUR 2,000 is paid
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The line manager approves business purpose, Accounts Payable pays the claim, and the employee is notified.

scenarios.name: Complete claim above EUR 2,000 is paid
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Both required approvals complete without prescribed order before Accounts Payable pays and notifies the employee.

scenarios.name: Incomplete claim is corrected and rechecked
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The same claim returns to receipt checking after employee correction.

scenarios.name: Required approval is rejected
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Accounts Payable records rejection, notifies the employee, and the claim ends without payment.
